title: A separated etale algebraic space over a scheme is a scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an algebraic space over $X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $q:E\to X$ be a morphism. Assume that $q$ is etale in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale morphism $V\to E$ with $V$ a scheme, the composite $V\to X$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume also that its diagonal $E\to E\times_XE$ is a closed immersion, meaning that every scheme base change is a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $E$ is represented by a scheme $Z$ over $X$, and $Z\to X$ is etale. No quasi-compactness assumption is made on $E$ or $q$.
